Question: For positive integers \(n,\) denote by \(D(n)\) the number of pairs of different adjacent digits in the binary (base two) representation of \(n.\) For example, \(D(3)=D(11_2)=0,\) \(D(21)=D(10101_2)=4,\) and \(D(97)=D(1100001_2)=2.\) For how many positive integers \(n\) less than or equal to \(97\) does \(D(n)=2?\)
